title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident shows a deliberate attempt to manipulate AI training data through content poisoning. A fictitious institution with no legal standing, no physical address, and no genuine researchers produced a large volume of text designed to resemble neutral academic work. The intent was for that text to enter the repositories from which AI language models draw training data, so that chatbots would reproduce its framings when answering questions about contested political topics. The failure mode is not one internal to any AI system but rather a vulnerability in the data pipelines that feed those systems: content that mimics credible sourcing can enter training sets without triggering authenticity checks.

The operation exploited the fact that AI systems cannot independently verify the institutional legitimacy of sources that look formally credible. Catching it would have required provenance checks on newly appearing organisations, scrutiny of abnormal publication rates, and verification that cited institutions actually endorse the conclusions attributed to them. None of those checks are standard in open-web data ingestion.

It is not established that any AI system's outputs were measurably altered, that the content successfully entered any specific training dataset, or that the campaign achieved its stated goal of improving AI responses to questions about Israel. The Guardian's reporting describes the operation and its intent, but whether it produced the intended effect on deployed models remains unknown.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

Israel established a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, funded and operated to promote pro-Israel messaging to artificial intelligence systems. Between August 6 and 14, 2026, the website published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words designed to appear as neutral academic research. The institute, which has no legal entity status or physical address, addresses controversial topics including alleged Israeli war crimes and genocide accusations by presenting arguments favorable to Israel while citing reputable sources like the UN and Amnesty International. The operation was part of a broader, multimillion-dollar campaign financed by the Israeli government through intermediaries including the advertising firm Havas Media and executed by companies including Piro Inc and Clock Tower X.

The campaign aimed to influence how artificial intelligence chatbots like ChatGPT respond to questions about Israel by seeding content into training data repositories. Israeli officials have privately expressed frustration that the expensive public diplomacy effort has failed to improve public opinion, with American support for Israel declining significantly since 2022. Researchers note the concerning implication that foreign governments and other actors may routinely attempt to manipulate AI systems through similar content poisoning tactics going forward.
